steps: A unique circle passes through any 3 non-collinear points (circumcircle)
4 or more general points need not be concyclic
check_code:
from fractions import Fraction as F
import itertools
# random-ish non-collinear points: check which n always admit a circle
def concyclic(pts):
    # solve circle through first 3, test rest
    (x1,y1),(x2,y2),(x3,y3)=pts[:3]
    a=[[2*(x2-x1),2*(y2-y1)],[2*(x3-x1),2*(y3-y1)]]
    b=[x2*x2+y2*y2-x1*x1-y1*y1,x3*x3+y3*y3-x1*x1-y1*y1]
    det=a[0][0]*a[1][1]-a[0][1]*a[1][0]
    if det==0: return False
    cx=F(b[0]*a[1][1]-a[0][1]*b[1],det); cy=F(a[0][0]*b[1]-b[0]*a[1][0],det)
    r2=(x1-cx)**2+(y1-cy)**2
    return all((x-cx)**2+(y-cy)**2==r2 for x,y in pts)
P=[(0,0),(4,1),(1,5),(7,3),(2,9),(8,8)]
always={n:concyclic(P[:n]) for n in (3,4,5,6)}
fits=[k for k,n in {'A':3,'B':6,'C':5,'D':4}.items() if always[n]]
assert fits==['A']
